Name: Godly Hand - Schedule Builder
Author: Aerishiph
Description:
GODLY HAND Schedule Builder — Sneak Peek Release [BETA]
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📌 Main Purpose

This is a sneak peek at another component of Godly Hand — a full all-in-one NPC creator coming to Nexus. This release is the Schedule Builder — the tool that replaces the most error-prone part of making a custom Stardew Valley NPC actually move around the world.

If you have ever written a schedule, you know what it is. It is a single long slash-separated string. Every entry is a time, a map name, an X tile, a Y tile, a facing direction, and an optional animation name, all jammed together, all in the correct order, all manually sorted by time because if they aren't sorted the NPC stands still. The internal map names are not obvious — HaleyHouse is not HaleyAndEmilyHouse, ScienceHouse is Robin's home, and the difference between Hospital and HarveyRoom matters. The time format looks like military time but is not — 2400 is midnight and is valid, 2500 is not, and nobody tells you that until the NPC vanishes at the wrong hour. The facing directions are numbered 0 through 3 but the numbers are not what you'd guess. And if you want the NPC to have a different schedule on rainy days, or when married, or on a specific day of the week in a specific season, you need to know that marriage_spring is the correct key, not spring_marriage, and that the game checks a specific lookup order you cannot see.

Then you test it, the NPC is frozen, and you start reading forum posts.

The Schedule Builder handles the string. You pick the variant key from a categorised dropdown covering every valid schedule key the game actually reads. You add time slots one by one — location from a labelled dropdown, tile coordinates from your coordinate finder, facing direction from a labelled picker, animation name typed exactly as it appears in your Animations.json. The tool sorts by time, assembles the slash-separated string, and outputs a Content Patcher-ready JSON. While you work, a live map preview shows you your NPC standing on the actual map tile, playing their actual animation, switching maps automatically as you scrub through their day. If something can't physically work — if the walk between two slots would take longer than the time you gave it — the tool tells you before you open the game.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

🗂️ Schedule Builder Features

[b]Every valid schedule key — all of them, organised[/b]

The schedule key is not just spring and summer. The game checks a specific priority order: exact date overrides first, then season plus day of week, then day of week alone, then rain, then the base season. For married NPCs it checks a marriage_ prefix version of each before falling back to the regular one. The variant picker covers all of it — base seasons, rain, all seven days of the week, all four season-and-day combinations (spring_Mon through winter_Sun), marriage equivalents of all of the above, and a custom key field for anything else. They are grouped into labelled sections in the dropdown so you are not reading eighty identical-looking entries. Import an existing Schedule.json and any key the tool recognises maps to the correct variant automatically. Unknown keys go into the custom field so nothing is silently dropped.

[b]Variant tabs — one at a time, not a wall of accordions[/b]

Each schedule variant — spring, rain, marriage_Mon, whatever you have — is a tab at the top of the builder. Click a tab and the editor switches to that variant's slots and its map preview simultaneously. The editor only shows one variant at a time. Adding a new variant opens it immediately. Removing the active tab moves focus to the nearest remaining one. The tab shows the slot count while collapsed so you always know which variants are populated without opening them.

[b]Slot editor with a column for every field[/b]

Each slot is a row: time, location, X, Y, facing, and animation. Time is a four-digit number in Stardew's own format — 600 through 2400. The location column is the full map dropdown with internal names and plain-English descriptions, the same list used across every other Godly Hand tool. Facing direction is a labelled picker, not a bare number. Animation is a free text field for your named animation entry. Slots sort by time automatically when generating, so you can add them in any order. The slot with the time matching your preview slider is highlighted so you can see exactly which entry the map is currently showing.

[b]Transit analysis — will your NPC actually make it[/b]

This is the thing nobody checks until their NPC teleports. When you have at least two filled slots, the tool runs a transit estimate on every consecutive pair in time order. For same-map transitions, it calculates the straight-line tile distance between the two positions, divides by a conservative estimate of two tiles per game minute to account for pathfinding overhead, and checks whether the remaining time after travel is at least thirty minutes. If it isn't, the pair is flagged with the exact gap that's missing — not just "something is wrong" but "this transition needs ninety minutes and you gave it sixty." Cross-map transitions can't be calculated because pathfinding through warp points is not knowable, so they show the time gap and a reminder to leave buffer. When you click Generate, any transit conflict surfaces as an amber warning above the button. The warning does not block output — it is an estimate, not a guarantee — but it is there before you load the game.

[b]Map preview — your NPC on the actual map, right now[/b]

Load up to four map files at once. Each slot takes a .tbin or .tmx file unpacked from XNB with xnbcli. Tilesheet PNGs are shared across all four slots — you upload your vanilla tilesheet pack once and every map draws from the same pool. Load your NPC's spritesheet PNG and optionally their Animations.json. The preview panel shows a live square viewport: your NPC standing on the correct tile for whatever time the slider is set to, playing their scheduled animation at the correct frame rate, facing the correct direction. Scrub the slider and the NPC moves. Switch to a different time slot and the viewport scrolls to the new position automatically. If the NPC is on a different map than what you have loaded, an amber notification names the map and the exact file to load. If no map is loaded at all, the notification still appears the moment a slot is filled, telling you which map file you need next.

[b]Four map slots with shared tilesheets[/b]

One map file per slot. Four slots total. As you scrub through the day and the NPC moves between locations, the preview switches to whichever loaded slot matches the current schedule entry's location. If you have Town, Saloon, SeedShop, and Forest all loaded at once, the preview cycles between them seamlessly as the time changes — no manual switching, no reloading. The active slot's card highlights green so you always know which map is currently displaying.

[b]The time slider uses Stardew's actual time format[/b]

The slider runs from 0600 to 2400 in ten-minute steps matching the game's clock. The live readout shows the raw game time value — 1330, not "1:30 PM" — so it matches exactly what you type into a slot. Tick marks at 0600, 1200, 1800, and 2400 give you orientation without false precision. The format is Stardew's own: hours times one hundred plus minutes. 2400 is midnight and is the cap. The tool validates this on generate and rejects any time above it.

[b]Asset checklist — always know what's missing[/b]

A small panel in the preview column tracks every asset in load order: the four map slots, the shared tilesheets, the NPC spritesheet, and the Animations.json. Each row shows a checkmark when loaded, an amber circle when something is actively missing, and dim text when a step isn't reachable yet. Map slots that have a file but are missing specific tilesheet PNGs name those files by filename. You never have to guess why the map isn't rendering.

[b]Import an existing Schedule.json[/b]

Already have a schedule? Load it. The tool parses every key and reconstructs the slots — time, location, X, Y, facing, animation — for every variant in the file. Known keys map to the correct variant tabs. Unknown keys go into custom entries with their original key string preserved. The NPC name field fills automatically if it's readable from the file.

[b]Warnings don't block output, errors do[/b]

Two classes of problem. Hard errors — missing NPC name, time values above 2400 — are red and prevent generating until fixed. Transit conflicts — the walk estimate, the short stay, the tight cross-map gap — are amber warnings that appear above the Generate button but do not block the output. The transit system is an estimate. If you have tested in-game and it works, the warning is noise and you can ignore it. The tool trusts you.

📥 Installation

This tool runs entirely in your browser. There is nothing to install.

[b]HTML version — recommended for most users[/b]
Download GodlyHand_ScheduleBuilder.html
Open it in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge
Done — no setup required

[b]JSX version — for Claude / React environments[/b]
Download GodlyHand_ScheduleBuilder.jsx
Drop it into Claude.ai or any React sandbox and run it

Both versions are identical in functionality. No internet connection required after downloading.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

📋 Requirements

[b]Map files for the preview[/b]
.tbin and .tmx are both supported. Extract base game maps from the Content folder using xnbcli or a Content Patcher bundle. Modded maps work the same way. The preview is optional — the schedule builder works without it.

[b]Tilesheet PNGs[/b]
Required for the map to render. Unpack the vanilla tilesheet XNBs alongside your map files. One upload covers all four map slots.

[b]Tile positions must come from in-game[/b]
All X/Y coordinates and facing directions have to come from actual play or a coordinate finder mod. Debug Mode and Tile Info on Nexus are both reliable. The tool structures your data. It does not invent positions.

[b]A modern browser[/b]
Chrome, Firefox, or Edge. No internet connection required after downloading.
